dedupe_keys.name: seismic resilience of a hospital emergency department in tuscany nonstructural damage and patient waiting time

description: This case study measures how well the emergency department of a hospital complex in Tuscany, Italy, would keep treating patients after an earthquake. Researchers at the University of Florence modelled both the building's nonstructural components, with special attention to suspended ceilings that failed in past Italian earthquakes, and the department's organisation. A metamodel relates these parameters to one service measure: the waiting time of yellow-code patients arriving in the hours immediately after the event. Resilience was then computed for earthquakes compatible with the seismic hazard of the site. The article is free to read and download as open access under CC BY 4.0 in the journal Modelling (2024). Coverage is one emergency department; the hospital is not named in the abstract. Caveats: facts here come from the article abstract, and no model code or data files are stated as available. Simulation uses: linking fragility of nonstructural elements to hospital service performance, and testing organisational measures that shorten waiting times after an earthquake. Related records: the 2023 Türkiye earthquake health facility damage study (case_study-turkey-2023-earthquake-health-facility-damage) is observed evidence on the same kind of losses.

name: Seismic resilience of a hospital emergency department in Tuscany: nonstructural damage and patient waiting time
organisations: University of Florence, Department of Architecture (DiDA)
outcomes: Quantifies the seismic resilience of the emergency department as the waiting time of yellow-code patients in the hours after an earthquake, for earthquakes compatible with the local hazard, with ceilings singled out as a critical nonstructural component.
resources_used: Metamodel linking nonstructural damage (notably ceilings) and organisational parameters to patient waiting time
